subject: Anthropology
title: Hegemony and Resistance
description: A quick, practical guide to Hegemony and Resistance.

hook.text: The ruling class doesn't need armies when people believe the system is fair. That belief is the real weapon.

buildup.text: Gramsci's hegemony describes how dominant groups maintain power by making their worldview seem like common sense.

discovery.text: Cultural hegemony operates through media, education, and religion — shaping what people think is normal and natural.

twist.text: James Scott found that the oppressed resist in hidden ways: gossip, foot-dragging, sabotage, and secret mockery.

climax.text: Power is never total. Even under hegemony, people find ways to push back — quietly, creatively, persistently.

punchline.text: Resistance hides where power can't see.

quiz.question: What is cultural hegemony?
options: Dominant groups making their worldview seem like common sense

details.summary: Antonio Gramsci's concept of hegemony describes how dominant groups maintain power not through force alone but by making their values seem natural and inevitable. Resistance occurs when subordinate groups challenge these naturalized assumptions through alternative worldviews and practices.
details.whyItMatters: Hegemony explains why people often accept inequality — dominant ideologies make existing arrangements seem natural. Understanding hegemony reveals that power operates through culture and consciousness, not just coercion.
takeaways: Hegemony makes dominant group values seem natural and inevitable
Power operates through culture and consciousness, not just force
Resistance challenges naturalized assumptions about social order

faq.question: How does hegemony differ from simple domination?
faq.answer: Domination relies on force. Hegemony operates through consent — convincing subordinate groups that existing arrangements are normal, natural, and beneficial. When hegemony works, people accept inequality as just the way things are rather than recognizing it as constructed and changeable.

faq.question: What forms can cultural resistance take?
faq.answer: Resistance ranges from open protest to subtle everyday acts — preserving forbidden languages, practicing banned religions, using humor to mock authorities, or maintaining alternative values. James Scott called these hidden transcripts — resistance conducted out of the dominant group's sight.
